title: Maze Generator
description: Build a maze generator using recursive backtracking, render it as ASCII, and solve it using BFS pathfinding.

steps.title: Create the grid as a 2D array of cells
steps.description: Define a `grid` as a 2D array where each cell is an object with `x`, `y` coordinates. Initialize a grid of the given `rows` and `cols`. Log the grid dimensions.
hints: Grid cell: { x: col, y: row }
Create rows * cols cells using nested loops

grid = createGrid(5, 5)
import json
print("Grid:", str(len(grid)) + "x" + str(len(grid[0])))
print(json.dumps(grid[0]))

verification.successMessage: Grid created with the correct dimensions and cell structure!
verification.failureMessage: createGrid(5, 5) should return a 5x5 2D array where each cell has x and y coordinates.

steps.title: Add wall properties to each cell
steps.description: Modify the cell to include wall properties: `north`, `south`, `east`, `west` (all set to `true` initially). Also add a `visited` flag. Log a sample cell.
hints: Cell: { x, y, walls: { north: true, south: true, east: true, west: true }, visited: false }
Visited starts as false (not yet explored)

verification.failureMessage: createCell should return a cell with all walls set to true and visited set to false.

steps.title: Implement recursive backtracking maze generation
steps.description: Write a `generateMaze` function that uses recursive backtracking to carve a maze. Start at (0, 0), mark as visited, choose a random unvisited neighbor, remove the wall between them, and recurse.
hints: Get unvisited neighbors (up, down, left, right within bounds)
Remove walls between current and chosen neighbor
Recursively call generateMaze on the chosen neighbor

verification.failureMessage: generateMaze should use recursive backtracking to visit all cells, carving passages by removing walls between adjacent cells.

steps.title: Render the maze to a string
steps.description: Write a `renderMaze` function that converts the maze grid to an ASCII string. Use `+`, `-`, `|` characters to draw walls. Log the rendered maze.
hints: Each cell is surrounded by walls on all sides
Middle rows: '|   |   |...' with walls shown as '|' or ' '

verification.successMessage: Maze renders with proper ASCII wall characters!
verification.failureMessage: renderMaze should use '+', '-', and '|' characters to draw the maze walls around each cell.

steps.title: Solve the maze using BFS
steps.description: Write a `solveMaze` function that uses BFS to find a path from the start (0, 0) to the end (rows-1, cols-1). Return the path as an array of `{x, y}` coordinates. Log the path length.
hints: Use a queue for BFS: start with { x: 0, y: 0, path: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }] }
For each cell, check neighbors where there is no wall between them
If neighbor is unvisited, enqueue with updated path
When reaching the goal, return the path

verification.successMessage: BFS found a path from start to end!
verification.failureMessage: solveMaze should use BFS to find the shortest path from (0,0) to (3,3). In an open grid, the path should be 7 steps long.
